guide.heading: Dragonlance Player's Guide
guide.summary: Krynn is a world where faith, magic, honor, and history all matter at the table. The Classic builder uses OSRIC as the foundation and layers Dragonlance sourcebook options on top.

cards.title: What makes Dragonlance different?
cards.body: Alignment has real story weight, divine power comes through Krynn's gods, arcane magic is watched by the Orders of High Sorcery, and knightly honor can shape a character's future.

cards.title: Available races and classes
cards.body: The builder supports the current campaign list: Krynn peoples, standard adventuring classes, Solamnic knights, student wizards, handlers, and tinkers.

cards.title: Progression-only choices
cards.body: Knight of the Sword, Knight of the Rose, and the robe orders are visible as goals. They are not level 1 starting choices because the PDF presents them as advancement paths.

cards.title: True clerics and druids
cards.body: Clerics and druids in Krynn draw power from the true gods. Their beliefs, alignment, and service matter more than in a generic dungeon campaign.

cards.title: Solamnic knights
cards.body: A Solamnic character begins with the Crown. Sword and Rose represent later acceptance, achievement, and story progression.

cards.title: High Sorcery
cards.body: Magic-users and illusionists begin as students or ordinary arcane characters. The robe path begins later, after the Test and a decision about magical allegiance.

before_building: Ask your DM which sourcebooks are active for your campaign.
Choose a race and class for the character you want to play now, not only for an advanced title later.
If you want a knight, begin with Knight of the Crown.
If you want a robe wizard, begin with Magic-User or Illusionist.
If you want divine magic, choose Cleric or Druid and discuss deity/alignment with your DM.

deities.heading: Deities
deities.summary: The PDF groups Krynn's gods into Good, Neutrality, and Evil. Clerics and druids serve through deity, alignment, and spheres of influence.

entries.name: Paladine
entries.portfolio: father of good, law, leadership, protection
entries.cleric_relevance: Major good deity and source of lawful good divine service.
entries.description: Paladine guides good through law, mercy, and mortal choice rather than constant direct intervention.

entries.name: Majere
entries.cleric_relevance: A contemplative good deity for disciplined spiritual characters.
entries.description: Majere favors restraint, patience, and inward mastery.

entries.name: Kiri-Jolith
entries.cleric_relevance: Important to martial clerics and the ideals of the Knights of the Sword.
entries.description: Kiri-Jolith represents battle in service to justice rather than conquest.

entries.name: Mishakal
entries.cleric_relevance: Strong choice for healing-focused clerics.
entries.description: Mishakal's faith restored knowledge of the true gods to many people after long darkness.

entries.name: Habbakuk
entries.cleric_relevance: Relevant to rangers, sailors, druids, and nature-minded divine characters.
entries.description: Habbakuk teaches harmony with living things and natural justice.

entries.name: Branchala
entries.cleric_relevance: A good deity for artists, wanderers, and celebrants.
entries.description: Branchala embodies the music of living souls and the creative spark.

entries.name: Solinari
entries.cleric_relevance: Not a cleric path in this guide; relevant to White Robe wizards.
entries.description: Solinari is the patron of the White Robes and good-aligned High Sorcery.

entries.name: Gilean
entries.cleric_relevance: Central neutral deity for knowledge and balance.
entries.description: Gilean stands between good and evil, preserving knowledge and equilibrium.

entries.name: Sirrion
entries.cleric_relevance: A neutral divine source for fire and creative change.
entries.description: Sirrion is passionate, elemental, and tied to the force of change.

entries.name: Reorx
entries.cleric_relevance: Revered by dwarves and gnomes; formal priesthood varies by culture.
entries.description: Reorx shaped the world and is tied closely to craft, invention, and the origins of several peoples.

entries.name: Chislev
entries.cleric_relevance: A strong deity for druids and nature-focused divine characters.
entries.description: Chislev is nature itself: living, wild, and balanced.

entries.name: Zivilyn
entries.cleric_relevance: A contemplative neutral path for wisdom-seeking characters.
entries.description: Zivilyn is associated with deep perspective and the wisdom of many times and places.

entries.name: Shinare
entries.cleric_relevance: Relevant to merchants, artisans, and civic-minded characters.
entries.description: Shinare governs trade, work, and prosperity created through effort.

entries.name: Lunitari
entries.cleric_relevance: Not a cleric path in this guide; relevant to Red Robe wizards.
entries.description: Lunitari is the patron of the Red Robes and balance-oriented High Sorcery.

entries.name: Takhisis
entries.cleric_relevance: Primary evil deity; evil divine service requires DM approval.
entries.description: Takhisis seeks rule and conquest, and her influence drives much of Krynn's great conflict.

entries.name: Sargonnas
entries.cleric_relevance: Known among minotaurs as Sargas.
entries.description: Sargonnas embodies vengeance, grim strength, and calculated brutality.

entries.name: Morgion
entries.cleric_relevance: Evil divine path; usually unsuitable for standard heroic play.
entries.description: Morgion is a solitary power of plague, decline, and hidden suffering.

entries.name: Chemosh
entries.holy_symbol: Worshipers are described with white skull masks and black robes
entries.cleric_relevance: Evil divine path; usually unsuitable for standard heroic play.
entries.description: Chemosh offers a corrupt promise of endurance beyond death.

entries.name: Zeboim
entries.cleric_relevance: A feared sea power; evil divine path needs DM approval.
entries.description: Zeboim is dangerous, unpredictable, and dreaded by sailors.

entries.name: Hiddukel
entries.cleric_relevance: Evil divine path; usually unsuitable for standard heroic play.
entries.description: Hiddukel tempts mortals through profit, deception, and bad bargains.

entries.name: Nuitari
entries.cleric_relevance: Not a cleric path in this guide; relevant to Black Robe wizards.
entries.description: Nuitari is the patron of the Black Robes and power-seeking High Sorcery.

classes.heading: Dragonlance Classes
classes.summary: These are the Dragonlance class choices supported by the current Classic campaign setup.

starting.name: Cleric
starting.overview: A true cleric of Krynn serving a deity through alignment and divine spheres.
starting.spell_table: Uses the cleric progression for the appropriate order of Good, Neutrality, or Evil.
starting.advancement_notes: Deity choice shapes available divine powers and expected conduct.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Discuss deity and alignment with your DM.

starting.name: Druid
starting.overview: A divine servant of nature and the Balance through Krynn's gods.
starting.spell_table: Uses druidic/nature divine magic as allowed by deity and campaign.
starting.advancement_notes: Best paired with a nature-oriented deity such as Chislev or Habbakuk.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Must fit the campaign's treatment of nature faith.

starting.name: Fighter
starting.overview: A practical warrior for soldiers, mercenaries, guards, and battlefield heroes.
starting.advancement_notes: Can remain a martial character or pursue campaign-specific orders later.
starting.campaign_restrictions: No special Dragonlance restriction in this guide.

starting.name: Ranger
starting.overview: A wilderness defender and scout suited to the plains, forests, and borderlands of Ansalon.
starting.advancement_notes: Works well for Nordmaar, Tarsis, Abanasinia, and frontier origins.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Confirm homeland and deity expectations with your DM.

starting.name: Knight of the Crown
starting.overview: The entry order of the Solamnic Knighthood, built around loyalty, obedience, courage, and service.
starting.advancement_notes: Crown service is the path toward Sword and eventually Rose.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Requires honorable conduct and acceptance of Solamnic expectations.

starting.name: Magic-User
starting.overview: An arcane student or independent caster before the robe path is decided.
starting.spell_table: Uses standard magic-user spellcasting until High Sorcery decisions apply.
starting.advancement_notes: The PDF notes that order choice is not determined before 3rd level.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Ignoring the Orders at higher level risks being treated as a renegade.

starting.name: Illusionist
starting.overview: A specialist arcane caster whose magic is folded into Krynn's wider High Sorcery structure.
starting.spell_table: Uses illusionist spellcasting as allowed by the campaign.
starting.advancement_notes: Before 3rd level, the Orders make no strict distinction between magic-users and illusionists.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Higher-level progression should address the Orders of High Sorcery.

starting.name: Thief / Handler
starting.overview: A stealth and skill specialist; among kender, handling is curiosity-driven rather than profit-driven theft.
starting.advancement_notes: Kender handlers are expected to create roleplay complications, not excuse hostile play.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Respect table boundaries around possessions and party trust.

starting.name: Tinker
starting.overview: A gnomish engineer-inventor tied to guilds, committees, devices, and a Lifequest.
starting.advancement_notes: Tinker play centers on devices, guild work, and improbable engineering.
starting.campaign_restrictions: Usually for tinker gnomes; race enforcement is handled by campaign agreement.

progression.name: Knight of the Sword
progression.overview: The Solamnic order reached after worthy Crown service.
progression.progression_note: Progression option, not selectable at level 1.
progression.spell_table: Gains clerical spell access later through Kiri-Jolith-oriented service.
progression.advancement_notes: Requires Crown advancement, petition, and story approval.

progression.name: Knight of the Rose
progression.overview: The highest Solamnic order, focused on wisdom, justice, compassion, and leadership.
progression.progression_note: Progression option, not selectable at level 1.
progression.spell_table: No separate player-facing spell table in this guide.
progression.advancement_notes: Requires proven advancement through Crown and Sword.
progression.campaign_restrictions: Unlocked by story, honor, and DM approval.

progression.name: White Robe Wizard
progression.overview: A robe order devoted to good magic under Solinari.
progression.spell_table: Uses White Robe spheres and moon effects after order entry.
progression.advancement_notes: Associated with good, protection, and Solinari.

progression.name: Red Robe Wizard
progression.overview: A robe order devoted to neutral magic under Lunitari.
progression.spell_table: Uses Red Robe spheres and moon effects after order entry.
progression.advancement_notes: Associated with balance, independence, and Lunitari.

progression.name: Black Robe Wizard
progression.overview: A robe order devoted to evil magic under Nuitari.
progression.spell_table: Uses Black Robe spheres and moon effects after order entry.
progression.advancement_notes: Associated with ambition, secrecy, and Nuitari.
progression.campaign_restrictions: Requires DM approval for player use.

high_sorcery.heading: Orders of High Sorcery
high_sorcery.summary: Krynn's arcane magic is governed by the three moon gods and the Orders of High Sorcery.

entries.title: White Robes
entries.body: White Robes follow Solinari and represent good-aligned magic. Their role emphasizes protection, responsibility, and the defense of magic from corrupt use.

entries.title: Red Robes
entries.body: Red Robes follow Lunitari and represent neutral magic. They often stand between extremes and are tied to balance, independence, and practical judgment.

entries.title: Black Robes
entries.body: Black Robes follow Nuitari and represent evil-aligned magic. They seek power and secrecy, and their use as player characters requires DM approval.

entries.title: The Test
entries.body: The Test of High Sorcery is a major threshold for arcane characters. This guide does not reveal Test content; it only notes that the Test marks the path into the robe orders.

entries.title: Moon Magic
entries.body: Solinari, Lunitari, and Nuitari affect their followers' magic through lunar phases. Low-level students are not affected in the same way as tested wizards.

entries.title: Progression Concept
entries.body: Begin as a Magic-User or Illusionist. Around the proper level and story moment, the character may face the Test and enter a robe order.

solamnia.heading: Knights of Solamnia
solamnia.summary: The Solamnic path is a story of honor, service, and advancement through orders.

entries.title: Knight of the Crown
entries.body: The starting Solamnic order. Crown knights focus on loyalty, obedience, courage, and the practical defense of honor.

entries.title: Knight of the Sword
entries.body: A later order for knights who have proven themselves through Crown service. Sword knights bind martial duty to spiritual and heroic ideals.

entries.title: Knight of the Rose
entries.body: The highest order. Rose knights are expected to show wisdom, justice, compassion, and leadership.

entries.title: Progression
entries.body: Sword and Rose are not level 1 choices. They represent acceptance by the Knighthood after service, experience, and story validation.

entries.title: Code and Roleplay
entries.body: Solamnic play is about conduct as much as combat. A knight's reputation and choices should matter in the campaign.

equipment.heading: Dragonlance Equipment
equipment.banner: These items are available only in Dragonlance campaigns.
equipment.summary: This section lists ordinary, cultural, and player-facing items only. It excludes artifacts, module rewards, dragon orb details, special magic item mechanics, and treasure secrets.

items.name: Hoopak
items.description: A kender staff-sling associated with travel, mischief, and personal style. Ask your DM for table rules before equipping one.

items.name: Kender pouches
items.description: Kender carry many pouches filled with found objects, keepsakes, and surprises. Use them for roleplay, not as an excuse to disrupt the table.

items.name: Tinker tools
items.description: Tinkers work with gears, pulleys, clockwork, waterwheels, and other mechanical parts. Device construction is campaign-managed.

items.name: Gnomish devices
items.description: Player-facing devices should be approved by the DM and treated as unreliable, experimental inventions.

items.name: Solamnic arms and armor
items.description: Ordinary knightly weapons, shields, armor, and heraldic equipment may be appropriate for Solamnic characters.

items.name: Medallion of Faith
items.description: True clerics begin with a sign of their faith. The story of how the cleric received it should be discussed with the DM.

equipment.omission_note: DM-only artifacts, adventure rewards, special magic item mechanics, and treasure secrets are intentionally omitted.

races.heading: Dragonlance Races
races.summary: These entries match the current builder race list. Advanced or rare peoples should be chosen with DM approval.

entries.name: Human
entries.culture: The most widespread and varied people of Ansalon.
entries.languages: Common and regional tongues by campaign
entries.roleplaying: Flexible origins, broad ambitions, and strong ties to the changing politics of Krynn.

entries.name: Kender
entries.culture: Fearless, curious wanderers with intense emotions and a talent for finding things.
entries.roleplaying: Curiosity and fearlessness should create adventure hooks, not player conflict.

entries.name: Hill Dwarf
entries.culture: Surface dwarves with strong clan identity and ties to trade, craft, and survival.
entries.roleplaying: Practical, stubborn, and shaped by dwarven history.

entries.name: Mountain Dwarf
entries.culture: Dwarves of great underground realms such as Thorbardin.
entries.roleplaying: Tradition, clan duty, and guarded pride are central themes.

entries.name: Qualinesti Elf
entries.culture: Western elves descended from Silvanesti, more open to the outside world.
entries.roleplaying: Balance elven heritage with practical engagement in the wider world.

entries.name: Silvanesti Elf
entries.culture: High elves with ancient traditions and a proud, formal society.
entries.roleplaying: Lean into discipline, history, and cultural pride.
entries.campaign_note: Confirm current campaign era and homeland status.

entries.name: Half-Elf
entries.culture: People between human and elven worlds, often shaped by divided belonging.
entries.roleplaying: A strong choice for characters navigating borders, cultures, and identities.

entries.name: Tinker Gnome
entries.culture: Gnomish inventors defined by guilds, committees, devices, and Lifequests.
entries.roleplaying: Build with exuberant overengineering and good humor.
entries.campaign_note: Best paired with the Tinker class.

entries.name: Gully Dwarf
entries.culture: Aghar survivors who thrive in ruins, refuse heaps, and hard conditions.
entries.languages: Common, Dwarvish, Aghar dialect by campaign
entries.roleplaying: Use carefully; the tone can become comic or tragic depending on the table.

entries.name: Irda
entries.culture: Rare, graceful, secretive descendants of ancient ogres with shapechanging lore.
entries.languages: Common, Irda, Ancient Ogre by campaign
entries.roleplaying: A rare people with major setting implications.

entries.name: Minotaur
entries.culture: Militant seafarers with a fierce honor culture and strong belief in strength.
entries.roleplaying: Honor, dominance, seamanship, and family reputation are major themes.

timeline.heading: Timeline
timeline.summary: A spoiler-light overview of the eras that shape player characters.

entries.title: Age of Dreams
entries.body: A legendary age of origins, first peoples, ancient wars, and the earliest foundations of elven, dwarven, human, and knightly history.

entries.title: Age of Light and Age of Might
entries.body: Civilizations rise, trade, build wonders, and eventually fall into pride and conflict.

entries.title: Cataclysm
entries.body: A world-shattering divine judgment ends the Age of Might, changes the land, and leaves generations struggling in darkness.

entries.title: Post-Cataclysm World
entries.body: True clerics vanish for centuries, old orders are blamed or broken, and communities survive through hardship, memory, and superstition.

entries.title: War of the Lance Context
entries.body: The return of dragons and armies of evil reshapes Ansalon. Player characters live in a world where the war's consequences are personal and political.

geography.heading: Geography
geography.summary: A short gazetteer for player orientation in Ansalon.

entries.name: Ansalon
entries.description: The southern continent that forms the main stage for the War of the Lance and most Dragonlance campaigning.

entries.name: Abanasinia
entries.description: A plains region with tribes, towns, and the communities around Solace and Haven.

entries.name: Solace
entries.description: A famous Abanasinian settlement and starting touchstone for many Dragonlance stories.

entries.name: Qualinesti
entries.description: The western elven homeland, historically tied to peace with dwarves and humans.

entries.name: Silvanesti
entries.description: The ancient high elven realm, proud and deeply traditional.

entries.name: Thorbardin
entries.description: The great dwarven mountain kingdom and one of Ansalon's most important underground realms.

entries.name: Sanction
entries.description: A harsh eastern city and strategic region connected to the wars of the age.

entries.name: Neraka
entries.description: A bleak central region associated with evil power and Dragonarmy activity.

entries.name: Plains of Dust
entries.description: A dry southern region suited to hard travel, nomads, and frontier danger.

entries.name: Palanthus
entries.description: A major northern city and center of civilization after the war.

entries.name: Sancrist
entries.description: An island region associated with the Whitestone and important councils.

entries.name: Mithas and Kothas
entries.description: Minotaur island realms with strong naval traditions.

entries.name: Tarsis
entries.description: Once a port, later stranded inland after the Cataclysm changed the seas.

organizations.heading: Organizations
organizations.summary: Player-facing organizations and factions without stat blocks or adventure secrets.

entries.name: Knights of Solamnia
entries.description: A chivalric order devoted to honor, goodness, and duty through the Crown, Sword, and Rose.

entries.name: Orders of High Sorcery
entries.description: The arcane orders that regulate wizardry through the White, Red, and Black Robes.

entries.name: Seekers
entries.description: A post-Cataclysm religious movement in regions such as Haven and Solace, important because true divine power had vanished from common life.

entries.name: Dragonarmies
entries.description: Militarized forces of evil that reshape the political reality of Ansalon during the War of the Lance.

entries.name: Whitestone Forces
entries.description: A broad alliance of good peoples and nations formed to resist the Dragonarmies.

entries.name: Elven Nations
entries.description: Silvanesti and Qualinesti preserve different elven traditions and political priorities.

entries.name: Dwarven Kingdoms
entries.description: Dwarven peoples are organized around clans, mountain realms, and old grudges.

entries.name: Minotaur Realms
entries.description: Mithas and Kothas are naval, martial societies built around strength and competition.

entries.name: Gnomish Guilds
entries.description: Tinker gnomes organize invention and work through guilds, committees, and Lifequests.

languages.heading: Languages
languages.summary: The PDF and current builder data point to the following player-facing language families. Final language choices remain campaign-managed.

entries.name: Common
entries.description: The broad trade and adventuring language used across many human and mixed communities.

entries.name: Regional human tongues
entries.description: Local languages and dialects vary across Ansalon.

entries.name: Elven tongues
entries.description: Used among Silvanesti, Qualinesti, Kagonesti, and related elven peoples.

entries.name: Dwarven tongues
entries.description: Used among hill dwarves, mountain dwarves, and other dwarven communities.

entries.name: Kenderspeak
entries.description: The kender language, often paired with Common for kender characters.

entries.name: Gnomish
entries.description: The language of tinker gnomes, guilds, devices, and technical explanations.

entries.name: Aghar dialects
entries.description: Gully dwarf speech varies by clan and community.

entries.name: Irda and Ancient Ogre
entries.description: Rare languages tied to Irda heritage and ancient ogre origins.

entries.name: Kothian / Minotaur
entries.description: Minotaur language used in Mithas, Kothas, and naval culture.

entries.name: Goblin and Ogre tongues
entries.description: Common among hostile or monstrous peoples; availability depends on campaign background.

entries.name: Draconic / dragon languages
entries.description: Known by dragons and some dragon-related creatures; usually not a casual starting language.
